messages:
Hanna: Hi payroll team — my Dec bonus landed in my SEK account but the paystub shows "US Supplemental Tax" withheld (SEK 15,000 withheld). I live and work in Sweden and have a Swedish bank on file. Any idea why?
Luis (Payroll): That isn't expected for a Sweden-resident. Can you upload the payslip and confirm your payroll country on Workday?
Hanna: Payslip uploaded to case PR-2026-1302. Workday payroll country = SE, bank = SEK account. Payline: Bonus SEK 50,000 gross; US Supplemental Tax SEK 15,000; Net SEK 35,000.
Svetlana (Intl Payroll): Thanks for the case. Quick note — sometimes equity/bonus elements routed through the global disbursement entity get a supplemental tax element used for US runs. We'll check the payout routing and element currency.
Ada: @Svetlana any chance this is related to the new payroll mapping we rolled out in Nov? I saw one config that mapped "bonus_global_usd" to the global element.
Svetlana (Intl Payroll): Good catch. If the bonus was posted using the "bonus_global_usd" element, the tax engine may have applied the US supplemental table. Action: we'll audit the payroll run, verify element used, and reverse any incorrect withholding. Please attach your bank FX confirmation if available.
Hanna: Uploaded FX confirmation. Case PR-2026-1302 has the docs. ETA?
Svetlana (Intl Payroll): Ticket routed to intl-payroll. Initial triage 3 business days. If we mis-applied withholding we'll: 1) post a correcting entry to restore net in next payrun or issue a one-time reimbursement, and 2) file remittance corrections with Skatteverket if required and reissue an updated income statement.
Luis (Payroll): Note for ops: we'll add a pre-flight check in the bonus upload flow to ensure element currency matches the payroll country.
PayrollBot: Case PR-2026-1302 created and assigned to team:intl-payroll. SLA: 5 business days.
Hanna: Thanks — leaving open until corrected :pray:
